cases.title: BufferCount 3 with Json=true writes exactly one 3-record JSON array per file
cases.intent: With Json=true the file target frames every flush as one JSON array: '[' + records joined by ',' and a newline + ']' + newline, and BufferCount alone decides when to flush. Downstream readers parse each file as one document, so a wrong count or a broken frame silently corrupts every batch. Two identical targets write the same records: F is read as JSON (exactly 3 records per file, gap-free sequence, Messages = 3 x Writes), R as raw text (the exact frame).

assert.comment: Read before the stop: every flushed file is '[' + exactly three records joined by ',' + newline + ']' + newline (FileTargetWriter.kt:278-296). Only the count flushes: BufferSize 16 KB and Interval 60 s are far away. Per-file counts read after the stop would include the partial batch an IPC service flushes on SIGTERM.
One put per flush carries Messages=3 and Writes=1 (FileTargetWriter.kt:226-227).

cases.title: BufferSize flushes on the first record that reaches the KB threshold
cases.intent: Without BufferCount the file target flushes when the buffered payload, a sum of String lengths, reaches BufferSize * 1024 (FileTargetWriter.kt:147). A 200-character constant pads every record to roughly 750 characters - far from both 512 and 1024 whatever the mode, marker or timestamp lengths - so one record stays below the threshold, the second crosses it and every file holds exactly two. If BufferSize were ignored nothing would flush within the 60 s default interval and the gate would time out. R, an identical twin, is read as raw text for the per-file count.

assert.comment: R is F's twin read as raw text before the stop: every flushed file holds exactly two records.

cases.title: An explicit Extension wins over the compression extension; a mis-cased Compression silently disables compression (known defect)
cases.intent: buildExtension uses the configured Extension when one is set, so A writes <uuid>.json.gz gzip files. Compression is a Gson enum with literals None/Zip/GZip; an unknown literal such as 'gzip' becomes null, compressionType falls back to NONE and B writes plain JSON with no warning - the operator asked for compression and silently gets none. Any correct fix (reject the value, or accept it case-insensitively) leaves no plain JSON in B's sink, which is what assertCorrect checks.

knownDefect.summary: An unknown Compression literal ('gzip') deserialises to null and silently means no compression

assertCorrect.comment: Either B is rejected (no files) or its output is compressed.

cases.title: A missing Directory is created on first flush; a target without Directory writes into the working directory (known defect)
cases.intent: T3 points at a directory that does not exist yet; the writer creates it on the first flush (FileTargetWriter.kt:245-248) - the docs never require it to exist, so that is pinned as behaviour. T4 has no Directory at all: the value defaults to Path("") and files land under the process working directory (the unit workdir), because the 'Directory must be specified' check in the dead FileTargetConfiguration.validate() never runs. dirFiles walks the unit workdir via 'dirs/..'.

assert.comment: createDirectories made <dirs/new>/not/yet/there/YYYY/... on the first flush.

knownDefect.summary: A file target without Directory is not rejected (dead validation) and writes into the process working directory

assertCurrent.comment: 'dirs/..' is the unit workdir, the cwd of every SFC process.

cases.title: ElementNames rename every output element
cases.intent: Top-level ElementNames rename the schedule, sources, values, value, timestamp, metadata and serial keys of every record, and the file target serialises with config.elementNames (FileTargetWriter.kt:137). Systems that ingest SFC output under their own schema rely on it. IPC mode is excluded here because the IPC target service never receives ElementNames; TGT-FILE-ELEMNAMES-IPC-01 pins that defect.

cases.title: IPC target services ignore ElementNames (known defect)
cases.intent: IpcTargetWriter.extractConfigurationForTarget builds the configuration an IPC target service runs with from AWSVersion, LogWriter, Metrics, Targets, Transformations, ValueFilters, TargetTypes, TargetServers, credential clients and secrets - not ElementNames, which the adapter side does forward. An IPC-hosted target therefore writes default element names and the same configuration produces different output in IPC mode. IPC mode only, by definition.

knownDefect.summary: IpcTargetWriter does not forward ElementNames to IPC target services, which then serialise with default names

cases.title: Custom formatter output is written verbatim, one formatter call per flush
cases.intent: With a Formatter the file target writes the formatter's bytes and nothing else: no JSON frame and no newline of its own (FileTargetWriter.kt:275-276). E2eLineFormatter renders 'E2E[<configuration>]|<marker>|<schedule>|<source>.<channel>=<value>' plus a newline; the configuration string a formatter receives is the target's own JSON (TargetConfiguration.targetConfig, TargetFormatterFactory.kt:20-23), proven by the target's Description reaching the file.

assert.comment: Exactly one formatter line per file: nothing before it, nothing after its newline.

cases.title: An unknown formatter class drops only that target
cases.intent: The formatter is created eagerly in the FileTargetWriter constructor (customPayload = formatter != null, FileTargetWriter.kt:56-60), so a ClassNotFoundException fails the writer's construction, which InstanceFactory reports as 'Error creating instance of' (InstanceFactory.kt:67). SFC carries on without that target: the gate keeps receiving every record and T's directory stays empty.

cases.title: Non-ASCII custom-formatter output is corrupted by the file target (known defect)
cases.intent: E2eLineFormatter returns UTF-8 bytes. FileTargetWriter.kt:276 maps every byte through toInt().toChar(), which sign-extends 0xC3 to U+FFC3, and re-encodes the chars with the platform charset, so 'Grüße °C' is never written as UTF-8 - on any JDK and locale. The string reaches the config as \u escapes, so the input itself is charset-independent.

knownDefect.summary: The file target maps formatter bytes through toInt().toChar() (sign extension) and re-encodes them, corrupting every non-ASCII byte

cases.title: Formatter and Template on one target are rejected at startup
cases.intent: TargetConfiguration.validate() refuses a target that sets both Formatter and Template, and sfc-main validates all targets at startup, so the process exits. docs/targets/file.md:88 says instead that a template is ignored when a formatter is used; the code is the behaviour, the docs are reported as wrong.

assert.text: Only one of Formatter or Template can be specified

cases.title: Compression GZip writes .gzip files that decompress to the JSON array
cases.intent: With Compression GZip and no Extension the file target streams each flush through a GZIP stream and names the file <uuid>.gzip (CompressionType.GZIP.ext, not '.gz'). The sink decompresses by magic number, so the records prove the content round-trips, and rawAbsent on the undecoded bytes proves the files are really compressed rather than plain JSON. R, an identical twin, is read as decompressed text for the frame.

assert.comment: rawAbsent reads the bytes as stored: deflate output never contains these literals.
R is G's twin, read as decompressed text before the stop: every file is a 2-record JSON array.

cases.title: Json=false batches glue records together with no separator (known defect)
cases.intent: docs/targets/file.md:103 says that with Json=false the output can be processed as plain text with individual JSON lines. FileTargetWriter writes the comma and the newline between buffered records only when the output is JSON-formatted (FileTargetWriter.kt:282-292), so with Json=false and BufferCount 3 each file is three objects glued as '}{' - neither JSON nor JSON lines. The raw text of every file pins the exact frame.

assert.comment: Whatever the separator, a flush starts with an object and ends with one newline.

knownDefect.summary: With Json=false the file target writes no separator between buffered records, so a batched file is '{..}{..}{..}' instead of the documented JSON lines

assertCurrent.comment: Exactly three objects joined by '}{', then the single trailing newline (FileTargetWriter.kt:296).
Two boundaries per file, at least four files.

assertCorrect.comment: One record per line group, each terminated by a newline.

cases.title: Json=false with BufferCount 1 writes one bare JSON object per file, newline-terminated
cases.intent: Json=false drops the array frame: a one-record flush is the record's JSON followed by a newline, with no '[' and no ']'. Consumers that read the files as JSON lines depend on exactly this. Two identical targets write the same records: J is parsed as JSON (one object per file, gap-free), R is checked as raw text.

assert.comment: Starts with '{' (no '['), ends with '}' and one newline (FileTargetWriter.kt:296).

cases.title: Non-ASCII string values are written in the platform charset, not UTF-8 (known defect)
cases.intent: FileTargetWriter.kt:253-255 builds its OutputStreamWriter without a charset, so the output encoding is the JVM default. CodeBuild runs corretto17 with LC_ALL=C (ci/cdk/lib/buildspec.ts:50, ci/e2e/lib/modes.py:211), whose default is US-ASCII: every non-ASCII character becomes '?'. JDK 18+ defaults to UTF-8 and would hide it, so the case pins the CI charset on every JDK with JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Dfile.encoding=US-ASCII. The value enters config.json as \u escapes, so the input does not depend on the charset.

knownDefect.summary: The file target encodes output with the platform default charset; under US-ASCII every non-ASCII character is written as '?'

cases.title: Output path layout <dir>/YYYY/M/D/H/M/<uuid><ext> and Extension normalisation
cases.intent: Every consumer that globs the output tree depends on the path layout: the file target writes <Directory>/YYYY/M/D/H/M/<uuid><extension> from Calendar ints, so month, day, hour and minute are NOT zero-padded (the docs' 'yyyy/mm/dd/hh/mn' at docs/targets/file.md:75 suggests otherwise). An Extension without a dot gets one, an empty Extension adds nothing. The regexes reject a leading zero in every component, so they hold on any date and would catch padding the day it was introduced.

assert.comment: An empty Extension yields a bare UUID file name.

cases.title: An IPC file-target service flushes its buffer when it is stopped
cases.intent: In IPC mode B runs in its own target service. IpcTargetServer registers a JVM shutdown hook that closes the writer within 15 s (IpcTargetServer.kt:94, :106-116), and FileTargetWriter.close() flushes (FileTargetWriter.kt:329-332). The runner stops sfc-main and then SIGTERMs the service; the sink is read after that, so exactly one file with all of B's buffered records proves the hook ran. IPC mode only.

cases.title: Records buffered in a file target are lost when sfc-main is stopped (known defect)
cases.intent: B buffers up to 1000 records or 1 MB and never reaches either. FileTargetWriter.close() would flush them (FileTargetWriter.kt:329-332), but sfc-main installs no JVM shutdown hook - only the IPC services do (IpcTargetServer.kt:94) - so SIGTERM drops B's buffer. File assertions read the sink after the runner has stopped SFC, so an empty B is the observed loss. In-process and uberjar only: in IPC mode B runs in its own service, whose hook flushes (TGT-FILE-SHUTDOWN-FLUSH-IPC-01).

knownDefect.summary: sfc-main has no shutdown hook, so a stop discards everything a target still buffers (FileTargetWriter.close() never runs)

assertCurrent.comment: Read after the stop: nothing was flushed.

cases.title: A Velocity template replaces the JSON framing; Int values reach the template as Double (known defect)
cases.intent: With a Template the file target writes exactly the rendered text: no '[' frame and no newline of its own (FileTargetWriter.kt:278, :296), and the template file's final newline is dropped by readAllLines+join (OutputTransformation.kt:45) - both pinned through the raw text of TT. The template renders a TargetData-shaped JSON object (with the docs' bracket notation: Velocity resolves $src.values to java.util.Map.values()), so TJ's records also prove the values and their order. Template data is the record re-parsed by Gson into a Map (OutputTransformation.kt:69), so the Int counter 3 renders as 3.0: a template cannot reproduce the record's own types.

assert.comment: fullmatch: the rendered line only - no '[' wrapper, no trailing newline.

knownDefect.summary: Template data is the record re-parsed by Gson into a Map, so every number is a Double: Int 3 renders as 3.0

cases.title: An unparsable template logs one error, then writes empty files counted as successful writes (known defect)
cases.intent: The template is parsed lazily on first use; a parse error is logged once and the template becomes null (OutputTransformation.kt:49-52). From then on transform() returns null, the empty payload is not buffered (TargetDataBuffer.kt:27) but the record still counts towards BufferCount, so every flush writes a zero-byte file and records WriteSuccess (FileTargetWriter.kt:147, :201-205). The data is lost while the metrics report success.

assert.text: Error creating velocity template from file template file
Error creating velocity template from file template file
assert.comment: The template is a lazy val: parsed, and the failure logged, once.

knownDefect.summary: A broken template turns every record into a zero-byte file that is metered as WriteSuccess

cases.title: TemplateEpochTimestamp exposes the nested epoch fields but not the top-level ones (known defect)
cases.intent: TemplateEpochTimestamp adds <timestamp>_epoch_sec and _epoch_offset_nanosec at every level of the template data, including the top level (OutputTransformation.kt:172-173). But only schedule, sources, metadata, timestamp and serial are put into the Velocity context (:86-95), so the documented top-level values are unreachable: $!timestamp_epoch_sec renders empty while the channel-level fields render.

knownDefect.summary: Top-level timestamp_epoch_sec/_epoch_offset_nanosec are added to the template data but never to the Velocity context

cases.title: A Template path that does not exist aborts startup
cases.intent: TargetConfiguration.validate() rejects a Template file that does not exist, and sfc-main validates every target as a TargetConfiguration before it starts anything (ControllerServiceConfiguration.kt:149), so the configuration error ends the process instead of surfacing at the first write.

assert.text: Target transformation template /nonexistent/sfc-e2e/e2e.vm does not exist

cases.title: Template tools: $date, $math and $tab exist; the documented $datetool does not
cases.intent: OutputTransformation registers the Velocity tools collection, math, context, number and date plus $tab (OutputTransformation.kt:99-106). docs/targets/file.md:127 and docs/sfc-target-templates.md:24 list $datetool instead of $date, so a template written from the docs silently loses its dates. This pins the code's names; the mismatch is a documentation defect, reported rather than pinned as a code defect.

assert.comment: $datetool is undefined (dt=N); $tab is a real TAB; MathTool.add(1,2) renders 3.

cases.title: UnquoteNumericJsonValues unquotes unsigned digit strings only
cases.intent: With UnquoteNumericJsonValues the serialised JSON is post-processed by the regex "(\d+(\.\d*)?)" (TargetData.kt:78-85, :110): the strings '42' and '3.25' become the numbers 42 and 3.25, while '-5' stays a string because the regex has no sign. Q, the same data without the flag, keeps all three as strings. strictTypes makes 42 and "42" different.

cases.title: File-target Interval and BufferSize ranges are never validated (known defect)
cases.intent: FileTargetConfiguration.validate() checks Directory, Interval 60..900 and BufferSize 1..1024, as docs/targets/file.md:99 documents, but nothing ever calls it: FileTargetWriterConfiguration inherits the empty validate() of BaseConfigurationWithMetrics, and the core validates targets only as the base TargetConfiguration. So T1 (Interval 1 s) flushes on a 1-second timer and T2 (BufferSize 0) writes one file per record, and neither range message is ever logged. The gate is a debug target so that a fixed validation of FILE targets cannot take the gate down with it.

knownDefect.summary: FileTargetConfiguration.validate() is dead code: Interval 1 and BufferSize 0 are accepted and used

assertCurrent.comment: Interval 1 s: the timer flushed at least once in the >= 3 s the gate takes.
BufferSize 0: payloadSize >= 0 holds after every record.

assertCorrect.text: Interval must be in range 60..900 seconds
BufferSize must be in range 1..1024 KB

cases.title: A failing file write is logged and counted as WriteError, never as a success
cases.intent: T's Directory lies below 'blocker', a regular file shipped in the case directory, so createDirectories fails on every flush - even as root, unlike permission-based failures. The writer logs 'Error writing to file' and puts the WriteError metric (singular, MetricsCollector.kt:320) instead of Writes/WriteSuccess (FileTargetWriter.kt:207-210). This is the signal the runner's noWriteErrors oracle relies on, so T is allow-listed here and every other case is protected by it.

files.blocker: a regular file: T's Directory lies below it

cases.title: Compression Zip writes one entry named <uuid>.json per file
cases.intent: With Compression Zip the file is <uuid>.zip holding exactly one entry, named after the file with a '.json' extension when Json is true (FileTargetWriter.kt:261, as docs/targets/file.md:78 promises). Tools that unzip the output rely on that entry name. The sink reads the entries, so the records prove the content and the sequence survives.

cases.title: Zip with Json=false writes an entry with an empty name (known defect)
cases.intent: FileTargetWriter.kt:261 passes "" as the zip entry name whenever Json is false, so every archive holds one nameless entry that common unzip tools refuse to extract. The content itself is intact (the sink reads entry bytes directly), which is why nothing else notices.

knownDefect.summary: Compression Zip with Json=false creates ZipEntry(""): the archive's only entry has an empty name

assertCurrent.comment: Every entry name is the empty string.
